rv.q: As a crowd-pleasing spectacle, it dutifully delivers.
A joyous telling of the arc of this sisterhood of talented performers — though the sound design drowns out about 50% of the lyrics.
Wraps the human stories of three icons inside an insanely fun, nostalgic package. Though it has some bumps to work out, as a world premiere it is in great shape.
Transforms a catalog of beloved songs into a deeply human story about resilience, sisterhood, influence, and legacy.
It is very good, and symbolically one hell of a way to go out — already stronger than most of its jukebox contemporaries.
Constantly struggles to effectively tell the overwhelming story of TLC, but it survives on the back of its galvanizing central trio and slew of hits.

cn.t: The TLC musical delivers powerful performances and moving moments of sisterhood, but critics are divided on whether it transcends familiar jukebox biomusical formulas to fully capture the group's legacy.
